How much should I budget for carpet installation in Renton, WA?

Plan on $4 to $7 per square foot installed, which covers carpet, pad, labor, new tack strip and haul-away of the old carpet. In practice that means roughly $600–$1,000 for one bedroom and $2,400–$3,900 for three bedrooms and a hall. The biggest variable is carpet grade, and you choose it at home from the full-size samples in the van — not from a display wall.
Does your mobile carpet showroom come out to Renton?

It does — Renton is home turf for us. The van arrives with 20+ carpet samples and all three pad grades, we lay them out in the rooms and stairwells they'd actually cover, then measure the whole house and write up your price on the spot. There's no store to visit, and the appointment costs nothing.
What does it cost to restretch carpet in Renton?

Restretching starts at $99 per room in Renton, and most rooms land in the $99–$180 range. A power stretcher pulls wrinkles, buckles and trip spots flat again for roughly one-fifth the cost of new carpet, which makes it the smart call while the pile still stands up and the color still works for you.
What do carpeted stairs cost in a Renton split-level?

Stair carpet starts at $18 per step, waterfall or cap-and-band, and a full staircase typically runs $235–$400. Split-level half-flights, landings and pie-shaped turns go into the written quote up front, never onto a later bill — in Renton that's most of our stair work.
How many days does carpet installation take?

One day covers most Renton homes. A split-level with bedrooms up, a family room down and the connecting stairs is a normal day's work for the crew; a large house with heavy furniture on every level can stretch into a second day. Your quote spells out the schedule before we start.
Do you move furniture, or do I?

We do the heavy part — beds, dressers, sofas and tables are moved out and put back on most jobs. You handle the small stuff ahead of time: closet floors, electronics, lamps, breakables and anything personal you'd rather carry yourself. Clearing those the night before keeps install day on schedule.
How do I know whether to restretch or replace?

Restretch when the pile still stands, the backing is sound and the color still suits the room — that's a $99-per-room repair instead of a whole new floor. Replace when traffic lanes are crushed flat, seams are letting go, the backing is breaking down, or pet odor returns after professional cleaning. We look first and tell you which job it is before quoting either one.
Which Renton neighborhoods do you work in?

All of them — Downtown, the Renton Highlands, East Renton Highlands, Kennydale, Benson Hill, Talbot Hill, Rolling Hills, Tiffany Park, Liberty Ridge, Maplewood, Cascade, Earlington, President Park and Fairwood, plus Skyway, Newcastle, Kent, Tukwila and the rest of South King County. On the edge of the map? Ask — the van travels.
What carpet holds up best with pets?

Solution-dyed nylon with a sealed backing, installed over a moisture-barrier pad. The barrier keeps accidents from soaking into the subfloor — the real source of permanent odor — and solution-dyed fiber can take diluted bleach without losing its color. The moisture-barrier pad upgrade starts at $0.65 per square foot, and samples of all of it ride in the van.
What warranty covers the installation?

OC Flooring backs the workmanship with a 1-year warranty, and the carpet carries the mill's own warranty on top — usually 10 to 25 years on wear and stain depending on grade. Both go in writing on your quote. Mills can tie their coverage to the pad underneath, which is one reason all three pad grades come along on the visit.
